headline: ETFs took $999M Monday; BTC's dip to $84,124 was bought back - profit-taking, not panic
summary: At 09:34 UTC on 22 September BTC is $85,885.20 against a $86,598 day open, ETH $2,738.93 against $2,775.49 and SOL $117.18 against $118.90 - all three down 0.8-1.5% on the day but still up 11.0-16.8% on the week, and each one sold off and was bought back rather than broken (BTC traded $84,124.00 to $87,446.70 and sits 53% up that range, ETH 31% and SOL 40%). The pullback has no news trigger behind it: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $998.95m on Monday 21 September - the largest day since 6 October 2025 and the ninth largest since launch, with IBIT $381.37m, ARKB $289.12m and FBTC $238.84m - while 24-hour liquidations ran only about $273.5m and were still 96% shorts, so this is profit-taking and leverage rotation after a 13% week, not forced selling. What did change since the 06:03 UTC briefing is that Hyperliquid open interest rebuilt instead of continuing to fall (BTC $3.92bn from $3.76bn, ETH $3.14bn from $3.11bn) and ETH's futures premium went back up to 0.077% from 0.044%, so fresh leverage is being laid on into a tape that is already extended. The macro backdrop is two-handed: US crude fell back below $100 on 21 September after Trump said he was open to talking to Iran at the UN, which is what lifted equities and risk assets, but the dollar is firm and the yen squeezed on rate-hike bets after the Fed's 16 September hike, with Williams, Jefferson and Barkin speaking today and Powell plus flash PMIs tomorrow. Mood is Greed on the composite at 66.4 while Fear & Greed sits at 78 in Extreme Greed and the 24h news tone is mildly negative at -0.404 - an extended market taking a breather near an eight-month high, with the real event risk (Xi at the White House Thursday, $16.6bn Deribit expiry Friday) still ahead rather than behind.

BTC.note: $85,885.20, down 0.82% from the $86,598 open and 1.79% under the $87,446.70 high, after a $84,124.00 low that was bought back about 2.1% - a $3,323 round trip with no headline attached to it; Hyperliquid open interest has rebuilt to $3.92bn from $3.76bn six hours ago with funding still flat and cheap at 0.00125%/h and the premium at 0.066%, and roughly 44,300 BTC have moved to exchanges since the rally began, so the supply pressing on this tape is holders taking profit into a $999m ETF bid rather than anyone being liquidated.

ETH.note: $2,738.93, the weakest of the three at -1.32% on the day and only 31% up its $2,707.90-$2,806.69 range, which makes it the closest thing to a real dip here; the warning sign is that its futures premium has doubled back to 0.077% from 0.044% at 06:03 UTC with open interest up to $3.14bn, so the leverage that got unwound in yesterday's squeeze has already been put back on, and spot ether ETFs were a net seller of about $140.6m in the week to 18 September against bitcoin's inflow.

SOL.note: $117.18, down 1.45% on the day and 2.33% under the $119.97 high but still the week's leader at +16.8%, sitting 40% up a tight $115.35-$119.97 range; it carries the thinnest book at $718m of Hyperliquid open interest and the highest funding of the three at 0.00182%/h, which makes it the most reflexive in both directions, and its ETF bid has cooled to roughly $60.7m in the week to 18 September from $153.87m in the week to 28 August, with Alpenglow mainnet activation on 28 September as the asset-specific event just outside the week.

drivers.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs bought $998.95m on Monday, the biggest day since October 2025
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $998.95m of net inflow on 21 September - the largest daily total since 6 October 2025 and the ninth largest since the funds launched on 11 January 2024 - led by BlackRock's IBIT at $381.37m, Ark's ARKB at $289.12m and Fidelity's FBTC at $238.84m, the third straight day of inflows. Scale matters for how far this dip can run: that single day is roughly 12,000 BTC and takes September to $1.31bn, though the funds are still down about $450m year to date, so this is a recovering bid rather than a completed one.

drivers.title: Today's pullback is profit-taking and leverage rotation, not a liquidation cascade
drivers.detail: 24-hour liquidations came to about $273.51m with $262.50m of that still shorts - a fraction of the roughly $1.01bn cleared in the 24 hours to yesterday morning - while more than 44,300 BTC have been sent to exchanges since the rally began, which reads as holders selling strength rather than leverage being forced out. The uncomfortable part is the other side of the same tape: Hyperliquid open interest rose again on all three majors in the six hours since the last briefing and ETH's futures premium doubled to 0.077%, so a second, freshly leveraged long position is being built into a market that is already 11-17% up on the week.

drivers.title: Fed day: Williams, Jefferson and Barkin today, Powell and flash PMIs tomorrow
drivers.detail: After the unanimous 12-0 25bp hike on 16 September - the Fed's first since 2023 - the dollar is firm and the yen squeezed on rate-hike bets, with Asian equities carried by tech rather than by rates. Today brings the Richmond Fed manufacturing index at 14:00 UTC with New York's John Williams at 14:05 UTC, Vice Chair Philip Jefferson at 14:20 UTC and Richmond's Thomas Barkin at 17:00 UTC, then Powell and S&P Global flash PMIs on 23 September (euro area 08:00 UTC, US 13:45 UTC) - the first full-month activity read since the hike. The stored history flags this exact channel: 'inflation/CPI' headlines preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.5% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.65x lift, n=118, held in both halves of the data).

drivers.title: Oil back under $100 after Trump opened the door to Iran talks at the UN
drivers.detail: US crude tumbled back below $100 a barrel on 21 September after Trump said he was open to talking to Iran at the UN, and falling oil and easing bond yields are what lifted Wall Street to within 1% of its record and carried crypto with it; this morning Trump added that Iran 'is not doing well' while Pakistan continues to mediate. The risk premium is only deferred, not removed: the February war ended in a Pakistan-mediated ceasefire and a June MOU that both sides have since violated, Tehran still demands an end to the naval blockade and unfrozen funds before restarting talks, and it continues to claim a right to control passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

drivers.title: Xi's state visit starts today; the summit is Thursday with the truce expiring 10 November
drivers.detail: China has confirmed Xi Jinping's state visit to the US from 23 to 25 September with the Trump meeting on 24 September - his first White House visit in over a decade - and the yuan has climbed to its strongest since 2023 into the talks. On the table are extending the Busan trade truce before it expires on 10 November, tariff cuts on non-strategic goods, Chinese rare-earth magnet flows and an AI-incident notification framework pushed by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, with Big Tech CEOs attending; wire coverage this morning describes tensions flaring over AI, trade and Iran even as both sides seek stability, so this is genuinely two-sided for risk assets rather than a scheduled positive.

drivers.title: Crypto-native newsflow is benign: Coldcard funds recovered, X adds trading, no new exploit
drivers.detail: White hats moved 52.37 BTC out of wallets exposed by the COLDCARD entropy flaw into a Crypto Recovery Trust address on 22 September, reaching the coins before the attackers and taking no bounty; that is about 2.8% of the 1,500+ BTC and $100m+ drained since 30 July in a bug that traces to a March 2021 firmware build, and Coinkite has already shipped emergency firmware. Separately X went live letting US users tap a $BTC or $TSLA cashtag and route an order to Coinbase, Kraken, Gemini, Interactive Brokers or Moomoo, with X acting as a connector rather than a broker. Neither is a market driver on its own - the point is that there is no live hack, depeg or exchange failure in the last 12 hours, which is why news_risk sits at 50 rather than higher.

watch.what: Richmond Fed manufacturing index, then New York Fed's John Williams at 14:05 UTC, Vice Chair Philip Jefferson at 14:20 UTC and Richmond's Thomas Barkin at 17:00 UTC. The first real read on how hard the Fed leans into further hikes after 16 September, and the most likely source of an intraday air pocket today.
BitMEX shuts down permanently. Balances and open positions still there have to move elsewhere - a small, mechanical liquidity event rather than a directional one.

US S&P Global flash PMI (euro area 08:00 UTC), the first full-month activity read since the hike, alongside Powell on this week's calendar. A hot services print is the cleanest bearish catalyst on the schedule.

Trump hosts Xi at the White House, mid-way through a 23-25 September state visit. A truce extension before the 10 November expiry removes a risk premium; a breakdown meets the Graham sanctions act signed 18 September authorising up to 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil.

Deribit quarterly options expiry, about $16.6bn notional ($14.73bn BTC, $1.92bn ETH), max pain near $72,000 - far below spot. Same day: Plasma's XPL cliff unlock of roughly $158m, some 63-65% of circulating supply.

Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation, cutting finality from about 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds. The largest protocol change of the quarter for SOL and the main asset-specific risk among the three majors.
BEA Personal Income and Outlays with the August PCE print, the cleanest test of the Fed's 3.7% headline / 3.4% core 2026 projections. Quarter end falls the same day and tends to pull flows around.

Context for any deeper pullback, from the stored history: BTC dips during greed got +1.5% back in 7 of 7 cases, ETH in 92.9% of 28 and SOL in 93.8% of 48, with a typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.3% to -0.5% and a median time to recovery of 3.5-5.0 hours. Today's market state most resembles 2025-07-14, 2025-10-04 and 2019-05-05, after which BTC's median 30-day move was +8.8% (up in 60.0% of them).
